headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty fell for the sixth consecutive week amid rising oil prices and global geopolitical tensions.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Crude oil prices spiked above $100 following Saudi Arabia's air raid warnings and export disruption fears.
Global market sentiment soured as North Korea declared its nuclear status irreversible, heightening geopolitical risk.
Investors reacted to the US Fed's hawkish stance, contributing to the sixth consecutive weekly decline.
Internal leadership uncertainty within the Tata Group created volatility across its constituent stocks.
whatHappening: Nifty 50 is hovering near a critical support level of 23,050 after a prolonged period of selling.
Goldman Sachs has identified HFCL and Polycab India as key beneficiaries of the global AI infrastructure boom.
Maruti Suzuki is pivoting towards a green future with a target to sell one million eco-friendly vehicles by FY27.
Market participants are closely watching Paytm as it remains in focus amid broader market turbulence.

summary: The Indian equity markets faced a challenging week, with the Sensex and Nifty recording their sixth straight weekly loss. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and crude oil surging past $100 per barrel weighed heavily on investor confidence. Despite the broader sell-off, specific interest remains in AI-linked stocks and Maruti Suzuki's aggressive green energy expansion plans.
